title: Learned selection yields a five-gene panel associated with early endometrial-cancer nodal status
summary: A study of early endometrial endometrioid carcinoma used random forests, sequential minimal optimization, J48 and Naive Bayes to develop a nodal-status panel from tumor sequencing and clinical data. Discovery used 24 hospital tumors and 289 TCGA cases; a separate 72-patient tissue cohort supported a five-gene PCR model. The reported combined panel AUC was 0.898, with sensitivity 88.9% and specificity 84.1%. The PCR cohort was also used for model construction/evaluation, so it is not a frozen-model prospective validation. Surgical-decision benefit and causal roles of the selected genes remain unestablished.
ai_technology: Random forest; sequential minimal optimization; J48; Naive Bayes
organization: National Chiao Tung University; Cathay General Hospital; Fu Jen Catholic University; Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen; Taipei Medical University

evidence.tested: 24 hospital tumors and 289 TCGA cases; new PCR measurements in 72 additional patients informed model construction/evaluation of a five-gene panel associated with lymph-node status.
evidence.unknown: No prospective frozen-model validation or demonstrated reduction in unnecessary surgery. Additional cohort measurements do not establish independent replication of a fixed diagnostic rule.
evidence.ai_role: Four learned classifiers selected and evaluated sequencing/PCR feature combinations linking tumor expression and clinical variables to observed nodal status.

source_review.scope: Independent complete primary Abstract; sequencing/model-selection and PCR-model Methods; relevant Results; visible publication/accepted dates and affiliations. No supplement review.
